title: wt restore-root result
description: The one document `wt restore-root --json` prints, on success, refusal and failure (nothing else goes to stdout). `wt restore-root` moves the branch the repository's primary checkout (the root) has checked out into a new linked worktree under .worktrees, carrying the root's uncommitted work, and puts the root back on the default branch. A root on a detached HEAD moves too (`detached` is true, `head` is its commit): when a local or remote-tracking branch already holds that commit the new worktree is left detached and no branch is made (`branch` is absent); a clean such root only switches to the default, with no worktree (`created` false, no `dest_path`, no `record`, `outcome` still `moved`: a consumer must not assume `moved` implies `dest_path`); when no branch holds the commit, `--branch NAME` creates NAME at that commit in the new worktree (`branch` is NAME, `branch_created` true) before the root is released. `outcome` is one of `moved`, `would_move` (a dry run: it would), `refused` (a check failed before anything was created; `created` is false; `already_default` is a refusal whose process exit code is 0) or `failed` (something went wrong after a write; `created` says whether the new worktree exists: when true it is KEPT, never rolled back, at `dest_path`, and `reason` names the state of the root and the step that stopped). `code` is the stable refusal or failure code (rescue's codes except `primary` and `nothing_to_keep`, plus restore-root's own); `reason` one sanitised line. `branch` is the root's branch that moves (for a detached root, absent, or the branch `--branch` creates), `default` the branch the root returns to, `dest_path` the new worktree (absent when none is made). `record` is the rescue record (ref under refs/wt/rescued/ and the commit it names) that held the root's uncommitted work before the root was reset; it is absent when the root had nothing uncommitted or none was written. `carried` and `left_behind` count what is (or would be) copied and what is not (ignored entries stay in the root). `default_ff` and `fast_forwarded` describe the optional fast-forward of the default branch to origin. `completed` lists the steps that finished (a benign note such as the default already being at origin appears here, not in `warnings`); `warnings` holds sanitised lines (always arrays). A run that failed before any outcome has `error` and none of `outcome`, `branch`, `default`, `dest_path`, `carried`, `left_behind`. The `detached`, `head` and `branch_created` keys were added without a version bump (version stays 1): a consumer that ignores unknown keys is unaffected. Branch names, paths and refs are raw identifiers carried verbatim: JSON escapes only C0 controls, so a consumer MUST escape them before printing to a terminal. Pinned to wt/internal/rootmove/json.go by wt/cmd/wt-session/restore_root_contract_test.go; a key or code added there must be added here and in the samples in the same change. Reuses the shapes of rescue-result.schema.json for `carried`, `left_behind`, `record` and `error`, which are unchanged.

code.description: Present for a refused or failed outcome. `already_default` is a refusal that exits 0: the root is already where it should be. `detached_root` now means a detached root whose commits are on no branch and no `--branch` was given. `branch_unneeded` (`--branch` on a root that is on a branch), `branch_invalid` and `branch_exists` are refusals; `branch_create_failed` is a failure creating the `--branch` name in the new worktree (the root is untouched).

created.description: Whether the new worktree directory exists now.

branch.description: The root's branch (short name): the branch that moves into the new worktree. For a detached root it is absent when a branch already holds its commit, and is the name `--branch` creates otherwise.

detached.description: Present (true) only when the root was on a detached HEAD.

head.description: Present with `detached`: the root's HEAD commit (full id).

branch_created.description: Present (true) only when `--branch NAME` was created in the new worktree.

default.description: The default branch the root is (or would be) switched to.

dest_path.description: The new worktree under .worktrees. Present once it exists (`created`) and in a dry run, where it is where it would be; absent when no worktree is made (a clean detached root that a branch holds).

default_ff.description: Present (true) only when origin/<default> is a strict descendant of the local default branch, so a fast-forward is possible; `fast_forwarded` says it happened.

fast_forwarded.description: Present (true) only when the default branch was fast-forwarded after the move. A fast-forward that is skipped or fails never undoes the move; the reason is a `warnings` line.

warnings.description: Sanitised lines. A line starting "record_not_written: " means the copy was verified but left no record. A line starting "root_held: " names the live wt session(s) holding the root: held warns (the move proceeds) and is never a `code`.

commits.description: Commits reachable from no remote-tracking ref (0 only when there are none; an unreadable count stops the run).

commit.description: Full commit id the record ref names.
